key: Error Correcting Codes + Phase Transitions + Self-Organized Criticality

concepts.name: Error Correcting Codes
concepts.short_description: Redundancy-based protection against noise; Hamming distance, Reed-Solomon, LDPC, turbo codes.

concepts.name: Phase Transitions
concepts.short_description: Abrupt qualitative changes in system behavior at critical parameters; universality classes, order parameters.

concepts.name: Self-Organized Criticality
concepts.short_description: Systems naturally evolve to critical states with power-law avalanches; sandpile models, 1/f noise.

hypotheses.statement: A decoder that is driven by slowly injected noise and relaxes between injections is a sandpile: unsatisfied checks are stress, bit flips are topplings. The decoding threshold (a phase transition) may be the self-organized attractor of such a driven decoder rather than a parameter someone tunes.

A system rewarded for throughput and punished for decoding failure will spend redundancy down until it sits at the edge of its code's threshold; the rate-noise phase boundary becomes an operating point reached by self-organization, and failures there come in bursts.

A medium at criticality has long-range correlations and so spreads any imprint nonlocally, which is what redundancy does; a critical medium may therefore act as an unengineered distributed code whose recoverability after local damage peaks at the critical point.

SOC is a noise source, not a mechanism of protection: a critical world produces power-law bursts of damage, and no fixed-depth code or interleaver suffices against scale-free bursts; codes that survive in a critical world must be multi-scale, and the need for a hierarchy of redundancy is the signature.

The abelian sandpile's recurrent configurations form a finite group equal to integer vectors modulo the graph Laplacian lattice; sandpile relaxation therefore computes a coset representative, i.e. a syndrome, for free. A sandpile is a syndrome computer for a lattice code whose codewords are toppling vectors.

Codes conserve parity the way sandpiles conserve grains: errors create defects in pairs and local decoders move and annihilate them. Bulk conservation is what makes sandpiles critical; parity conservation might make driven local decoders critical, and breaking it should remove the criticality.

A population whose genomes carry evolvable redundancy under mutation has an error threshold (a phase transition in heredity); if redundancy costs fitness, the population self-organizes to the edge of that threshold, with extinction and sweep events of scale-free size.

Syndrome sandpile: on a sparse Tanner graph, noise is injected one bit at a time and a threshold bit-flip rule (flip a variable when at least t of its checks are unsatisfied) runs to quiescence between injections. The stationary residual-error density self-tunes toward the ensemble's bit-flip decoding threshold, because below it relaxation removes errors and above it stalled trapping sets accumulate and flips create new errors.

hypotheses.statement: Redundancy thermostat: a storage agent lowers its protection (scrub effort or transmit power) by a small step after every successful epoch and raises it by a large step after every failure, with residual errors persisting between epochs. The operating point is driven to the edge of the scrubbing threshold and failures arrive in heavy-tailed bursts because persistent residue couples consecutive epochs.

hypotheses.statement: Sandpile syndrome computer: take the graph Laplacian lattice as a lattice code (codewords = integer toppling vectors times the reduced Laplacian). Relaxing a received grain vector to its recurrent representative computes its coset, i.e. its syndrome, by purely local threshold dynamics; decoding reduces to a lookup from recurrent configuration to minimum-weight grain error.

hypotheses.statement: Error-threshold seeking: genomes carry an evolvable repetition factor on their functional bits; redundancy costs replication speed. hypotheses.statement: Scale-free burst memory: marks written into a sandpile are erased when their site topples. At criticality erasures come in spatially compact bursts of every size, so the benefit of scattering an erasure-code's symbols (interleaving) over placing them contiguously grows with system size, whereas in a subcritical pile the benefit saturates once the spread exceeds the characteristic avalanche size.

hypotheses.statement: Parity-conserving lazy decoder: on a planar surface-code-like lattice, edge flips create defect pairs; a lazy local decoder acts only where a neighbourhood holds at least theta defects, and its moves either annihilate adjacent pairs or hop a defect (parity preserving). Defects leave only at the boundary. Parity conservation plus threshold laziness plus boundary-only loss should make decoding avalanches scale-free; allowing bulk single-defect deletion should destroy it.

hypotheses.statement: Miscorrection contagion: a network of storage nodes each scrubs its own codeword, but a miscorrection at one node leaks corrupted symbols into its neighbours' codewords. The branching ratio of miscorrection set by code distance and coupling determines whether failures stay local or cascade, and repair policies that reduce scrub effort after quiet periods poise the network at branching ratio one.

lenses.name: Syndrome-grain bookkeeping
lenses.rationale: Treat unsatisfied checks as grains and decoder moves as topplings so that sandpile statistics can be computed on decoders directly.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series of decoder moves per injection, with the defect/unsatisfied-check set before and after each move
lenses.transformation: segment into avalanches (moves between consecutive injections), compute size, duration, area, and branching ratio (moves caused per move)
observables: 95th-percentile size s95 as a function of system size
predictedSignals: s95 grows with system size roughly as a power
branching ratio near 1 in the conserving rule
lenses.nullExpectation: sizes have a characteristic scale independent of system size; branching ratio clearly below 1
failureModes: finite-size cutoff dominates at small L
log-log straightness mistaken for power law
overlapping avalanches when drive is not slow
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: makes decoders measurable with sandpile statistics rather than only with failure rates

lenses.name: Threshold-distance thermometer
lenses.rationale: Any claim that a dynamics sits 'at threshold' needs an independent threshold measurement made without the dynamics.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: block failure probability versus iid noise rate p for two block lengths of the same ensemble
lenses.transformation: fit logistic curves, locate the crossing of the two curves as p*; express any operating point as (p - p*)/p*
observables: relative distance of self-organized operating points to p*
lenses.nullExpectation: operating points unrelated to p* (e.g. near zero or far above)
failureModes: curves do not cross at small n
bit-flip decoder threshold poorly defined for small blocks
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: an external reference point, so that 'critical' is not self-certified by the dynamics being tested

lenses.name: Interleaver-depth demand curve
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: the burst law of a critical world should show up as a growing demand for spread in a code's layout, which is a code-side measurement of criticality.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: survival time of a k-of-n erasure-coded message under a given layout in a given burst world
lenses.transformation: compute median survival for contiguous and scattered layouts, and the minimal spread radius that reaches 90% of scattered-layout survival, as a function of system size L
observables: survival ratio R(L) = median survival scattered / contiguous
predictedSignals: R(L) and D(L) increase with L at criticality
both saturate in a subcritical world
R near 1 in an iid world
lenses.nullExpectation: R(L) flat in L in all regimes
failureModes: mean avalanche area growth alone drives R(L) growth
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: measures criticality through its consequence for information retention rather than through avalanche histograms

lenses.name: Coset ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: view every sandpile configuration by its coset modulo the Laplacian lattice so that relaxation is read as syndrome computation.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: integer grain vectors on non-sink vertices of a small graph
lenses.transformation: map each vector to its recurrent representative by stabilisation plus the identity-element trick; tabulate minimum-weight error per coset by breadth-first enumeration
observables: minimum L1 weight of a nonzero lattice vector
predictedSignals: decoding success curve sharpens with graph size within a family
lenses.nullExpectation: success curve shape unchanged by graph size
failureModes: cosets too many to tabulate beyond ~16 vertices
lattice minimum distance fixed by vertex degree so no family scaling
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: gives the sandpile an algebraic code reading independent of avalanche statistics

lenses.name: Defect-parity audit
lenses.rationale: Tests the analogy grain conservation <-> parity conservation directly by counting where parity is broken.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: defect set per time step with a region partition
lenses.transformation: compute per-region defect-parity changes not accounted for by boundary crossings
observables: correlation of violation rate with avalanche cutoff exponent
predictedSignals: zero violations in the conserving rule, with the largest cutoff scaling
cutoff scaling falls as bulk violation rate rises
lenses.nullExpectation: cutoff scaling independent of violation rate
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: isolates the conservation ingredient rather than treating the decoder rule as a black box

lenses.name: Residue-cluster geometry
lenses.rationale: Failure residue that is critical should have fractal, system-spanning clusters; failure residue that is a mixture should have compact, bounded clusters.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: set of wrong bits after relaxation, embedded in the Tanner graph or lattice
lenses.transformation: connected components in the graph induced by wrong bits and their shared checks; size and graph-diameter per component
predictedSignals: largest component fraction rises sharply near p*
broad component-size distribution only near p*
lenses.nullExpectation: components are those of iid errors at the same density
failureModes: expander-like Tanner graphs make diameter uninformative
density matching of iid null is approximate
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: looks at the spatial form of residue, not only its count

lenses.name: Inter-failure clock
lenses.rationale: Separates a controller parked at a quantile (memoryless failures) from a system with memory-coupled bursts.
lenses.transformation: inter-failure interval distribution, Fano factor of failure counts in windows of 10, 100, 1000 epochs
predictedSignals: Fano factor grows with window size when residue couples epochs
lenses.nullExpectation: Fano factor near 1 at all windows (Bernoulli failures)
failureModes: controller oscillation produces clustering without criticality
short runs make large-window Fano noisy
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: a temporal-memory test that does not rely on spatial avalanche definitions

experiments.hypothesis: A lazy, parity-conserving local decoder on a planar parity-check lattice under slow edge-flip drive produces decoding avalanches whose size cutoff scales with lattice size; permitting bulk single-defect deletion, at a rate matched to give the same mean avalanche size, removes that scaling.
experiments.mechanism: LxL planar lattice, errors on edges, vertex parity checks give defects. Drive: flip one uniformly random edge, then relax. Relaxation: any vertex whose 3x3 neighbourhood holds >= theta=3 defects is active; an active vertex either annihilates an adjacent defect pair by flipping the connecting edge or moves one of its defects one step toward the nearest lattice boundary (random tie-breaks). Defects reaching a boundary are removed. Relax until no active vertex.
experiments.intervention: null twin rule: identical, plus each active step deletes a bulk defect without flipping an edge with probability eps, eps calibrated by bisection so mean avalanche size matches the conserving rule within 5%
experiments.control: eager decoder theta=1 (no stress accumulation) at the same sizes
experiments.positive_control: 2D BTW sandpile at L=16,32,64 through the same avalanche-analysis code must give s95(64)/s95(16) >= 4
experiments.observable: s95 (95th percentile avalanche size in edge flips) per L; bulk parity-violation count; logical-failure count (boundary-to-boundary error chain) per 1000 injections
experiments.success_criterion: conserving rule: s95(L=64)/s95(L=16) >= 4 AND null twin: s95(64)/s95(16) <= 2, both with 4-seed bootstrap 90% intervals not overlapping
experiments.failure_criterion: conserving rule s95(64)/s95(16) < 2, OR null twin ratio within the conserving rule's 90% interval, OR positive control fails (then the run is void, not a failure)
experiments.alternative_explanation: cutoff growth comes from boundary distance alone (defects travel farther in bigger lattices) rather than from conservation-driven criticality; checked by the null twin, which keeps boundaries
experiments.null_twin: bulk-deletion twin matched on mean avalanche size and identical drive, lattice and boundaries; destroys parity conservation only
experiments.why_this_implementation: a plain lattice with explicit parity checks keeps the code structure visible (defects, logical chains); a cellular-automaton formulation was displaced because synchronous updates would obscure the drive/relax separation that defines SOC
experiments.size: L in {16, 32, 64}; 2000 burn-in + 20000 measured injections per run; 4 seeds; 3 rules (conserving, bulk-deletion twin, eager) plus BTW positive control
stupid_explanations: defects walking to the boundary take ~L steps, so any size measure grows with L regardless of criticality
the laziness threshold creates a backlog that is released in big clearances simply because the lattice fills, not because the state is critical
eps calibration matches the mean but not the variance, so the twin differs in more than conservation

experiments.hypothesis: Under one-bit-at-a-time noise injection with bit-flip relaxation to quiescence, the stationary residual-error density of a regular (3,6) sparse code sits within 20% of the independently measured bit-flip threshold of the same ensemble.
experiments.mechanism: random (3,6)-regular Tanner graph, all-zero codeword, error vector e. Drive: flip one random bit of e. Relax: parallel sweeps flipping every variable with >= 2 of 3 checks unsatisfied, up to 50 sweeps or quiescence. Record residual density |e|/n after each relaxation.
experiments.intervention: null twin: same injection, but relaxation flips a uniformly random set of variables of the same size as the syndrome rule would have flipped at that step (syndrome-blind)
experiments.control: fast drive: inject 10 bits per relaxation instead of 1
experiments.positive_control: L2 threshold measurement: iid errors at p in a grid of 20 values, 200 blocks each, n in {1000, 2000}; crossing must exist in [0.01, 0.2] or the run is void
experiments.observable: stationary density rho* = mean of |e|/n over the last half of injections; drift slope of |e|/n over the last half; L2 threshold p*
experiments.success_criterion: |rho* - p*|/p* <= 0.2 AND drift slope over last half < 0.05 * rho* per 10^4 injections (stationary) AND null twin |rho*_twin - p*|/p* > 0.5
experiments.failure_criterion: rho* < 0.2 p* (decoder simply cleans up), OR non-stationary drift above the bound (trapping-set accumulation), OR null twin also within 20% of p*
experiments.alternative_explanation: any threshold decoder driven slowly will park at a density where flip-in equals flip-out, which could coincide with p* by accident of the degree profile; tested by repeating at t=3-of-3 whose threshold differs
experiments.null_twin: syndrome-blind relaxation with matched flip counts; destroys the parity-driven mechanism while preserving drive and flip volume
experiments.why_this_implementation: a Tanner graph with a threshold flip rule is the literal code; a neural decoder was not considered because the question is about the code's own dynamics
experiments.size: n in {1000, 2000}; 30000 injections per run; 3 seeds; threshold sweep 20 p-values x 200 blocks x 2 n
stupid_explanations: residue accumulates in trapping sets monotonically and the density 'at' p* is just where the run was stopped
the density equals p* because both are set by the same degree-3 majority arithmetic, not by self-organization
the twin fails merely because random flips inject errors, a trivially different drive

experiments.hypothesis: In a critical sandpile the survival advantage of scattered over contiguous placement of an erasure code's symbols grows with system size, while in a subcritical pile it saturates and in an iid-erasure world it is absent.
experiments.mechanism: 2D BTW sandpile LxL, open boundaries, driven one grain at a time after burn-in. A message is one (n=32, k=16) erasure codeword: 32 symbols pinned at 32 sites; a symbol is erased the first time its site topples. The message dies when more than 16 symbols are erased. Layouts: contiguous 4x8 block at a random position, or 32 uniformly scattered sites.
experiments.intervention: subcritical regime: each toppling loses a grain in the bulk with probability 0.05; iid twin: each site is erased per grain added with probability equal to that site class's empirical per-grain toppling probability measured in the critical run
experiments.control: same pipeline with k=32 of n=32 (no redundancy): layout should matter less
experiments.positive_control: iid twin must give R within [0.9, 1.1], confirming layout is irrelevant without spatial correlation
experiments.observable: R(L) = median survival (in grains added) of scattered / contiguous layouts, per regime and L
experiments.success_criterion: critical: R(64)/R(16) >= 1.5; subcritical: R(64)/R(16) <= 1.15; iid: R within [0.9, 1.1] at both L; 400 messages per cell, bootstrap 90% intervals non-overlapping between critical and subcritical ratios
experiments.failure_criterion: critical R(64)/R(16) < 1.2, OR subcritical ratio within the critical ratio's 90% interval, OR iid positive control out of range (void)
experiments.alternative_explanation: R grows with L because contiguous blocks of fixed 4x8 size become a smaller fraction of a growing avalanche's area, which holds for any correlated erasure law whose mean area grows with L; the subcritical arm is what separates this
experiments.null_twin: iid erasures matched on per-site erasure rate; destroys spatial burst structure
experiments.why_this_implementation: a threshold-toppling grid is the minimal generator of scale-free compact bursts; a cellular-automaton reading is possible but the sequential drive/relax loop is kept explicit rather than recast as a CA
experiments.size: L in {16, 32, 64}; 400 messages per layout x regime x L (messages overlaid on shared runs, 8 per run); 3 regimes; 2 seeds of sandpile history
stupid_explanations: sites near the boundary topple less, and scattered layouts oversample the boundary
contiguous blocks are wiped by a single avalanche at any size; survival differences reflect block size, not burst law
the subcritical arm has a much lower toppling rate, so its survival times are longer and ratios compress

experiments.hypothesis: A storage scrubber that lowers effort after each clean epoch and raises it after each failure, with residual errors persisting between epochs, shows failure clustering (Fano factor growing with window) beyond a memoryless twin driven by the same measured failure curve.
experiments.mechanism: (3,6)-regular code n=1000 stored in a noisy memory; each epoch adds iid bit flips at p=0.02; scrub = s sweeps of bit-flip (s is the effort, integer 1..20); failure = residual errors > 0 after scrub; residual errors persist. Update: s -= 1 after 20 consecutive clean epochs, s += 3 after a failure.
experiments.intervention: memoryless twin: at each epoch failure is Bernoulli(Pfail(s)) with Pfail(s) measured from fresh-start scrubs at each s; same update rule
experiments.control: fixed effort at the adaptive run's median s
experiments.positive_control: a synthetic failure stream with injected clustering (Markov-modulated Bernoulli, burst prob 0.3) must produce Fano(1000)/Fano(10) >= 3 through the same L7 code
experiments.observable: Fano factor of failure counts at windows 10, 100, 1000 epochs; mean effort; time-averaged residual density
experiments.success_criterion: adaptive: Fano(1000)/Fano(10) >= 2 AND memoryless twin: Fano(1000)/Fano(10) <= 1.3, 3 seeds each, all seeds agreeing in direction
experiments.failure_criterion: adaptive and twin ratios both within 1.3x of each other, in which case M2 is recorded as a plain controller
experiments.alternative_explanation: the asymmetric step rule creates sawtooth effort oscillations that cluster failures regardless of residue coupling; the memoryless twin shares the rule and controls for this
experiments.null_twin: memoryless Bernoulli failures with the same effort-to-failure curve and the same update rule; destroys the persistent-residue coupling
experiments.why_this_implementation: a scalar effort controller around a real scrub decoder is the minimal form; a reinforcement-learning agent was displaced because the question is whether the code's persistence creates memory, not whether a learner finds a policy
experiments.size: n=1000; 60000 epochs per run; 3 seeds; Pfail(s) calibration 20 s-values x 300 fresh starts
stupid_explanations: the sawtooth controller clusters failures on its own
Pfail(s) measured from fresh starts underestimates failure with residue, so the twin runs at a different operating point
residue grows without bound and the run is nonstationary, which inflates large-window Fano trivially
